title: The Doctor's Midnight Rounds: Angoda's Unseen Superintendent
description:
Deep within the hushed corridors of Angoda's National Institute of Mental Health, some say a presence still lingers. This episode of Ceylon Dread delves into the chilling urban legend of 'The Doctor's Midnight Rounds,' a tale whispered among staff and patients alike.

Join us as we recount the unnerving experiences of Ruvini, a young nurse, who encountered the phantom footsteps and jingle of keys belonging to a long-dead superintendent, forever patrolling his silent wards.
fiction_note: Based on Sri Lankan urban legends; characters and events are dramatised.

scenes.narration: Have you ever walked down a long, quiet corridor at night... and felt a breath of air that wasn't there? A sudden chill that has nothing to do with the temperature outside? In Sri Lanka, especially in older places, some corridors hold more than just shadows. Angoda, the National Institute of Mental Health, is one such place. Its walls have seen much. Old Nurse Leela, she always said, "The walls, they remember, putha. Everything." For Ruvini, a young nurse newly transferred, Angoda was just a job. A quiet, demanding job, with the scent of disinfectant and the distant hum of the city. She would soon learn that some duties extend beyond the living.
visuals: Exterior of an old, colonial-era hospital building at dusk, overgrown creepers on stone walls, warm light spilling from a few windows, 50mm lens, cinematic.
A dimly lit, empty hospital corridor, fluorescent lights flickering weakly, long shadows stretching from pillars, wet ground after rain, 35mm film grain.

scenes.narration: It was during her first few night shifts that the whispers began. Softly, around the nurses' station, over cups of sweet, strong tea. "The Midnight Rounds," they called it. Nurse Leela, her eyes kind but knowing, had cautioned Ruvini. "Don't mind the stories, putha, but always be aware. Some presences... they don't know it's time to leave." Ruvini, fresh from training, tried to dismiss it as old wives' tales, the kind grandmothers tell to keep children in bed. A way to pass the long, silent hours. But the way Leela said it, the quiet certainty in her voice, it settled in Ruvini's mind, like a seed planted in the dark.
visuals: Two nurses (backs to camera) sharing tea at a worn wooden table in a dimly lit staff room, a kerosene lamp on the table, 85mm lens, shallow depth of field.
An old, framed black-and-white photograph of a stern-looking man in a doctor's coat, hanging on a peeling hospital wall, dust motes in the faint light, close-up.

scenes.narration: Ruvini's first few midnight rounds were uneventful. Just the soft creak of her shoes on the polished linoleum, the distant sound of geckos chirping. The hum of the old fluorescent tubes above, a lullaby of the night. She checked on patients, adjusted IVs, updated charts. The older wards, especially, had a particular quietness. A heavy, almost watchful silence. Sometimes, she would glance down the long, empty corridors, expecting to see a security guard, or another nurse. But there was only the play of shadows, shifting with the weak light, and the occasional sigh of the building itself, settling in for the night.
visuals: A long, empty hospital ward, rows of old metal beds with white sheets, moonlight streaming faintly through high windows, creating stark shadows, wide shot, 24mm lens.
Ruvini's back as she bends over a patient chart, her silhouette against a softly lit room, a single, old-fashioned medical lamp on a nearby table, soft focus.

scenes.narration: Then, one night, it started. A faint, dragging sound. A shuffle, far down Ward C, one of the oldest, emptiest sections. Ruvini paused, her pen hovering over a chart. "Just the wind," she told herself, glancing at the sealed windows. "Or old pipes." The hospital was an ancient beast, full of its own groans and whispers. She shook her head, trying to dismiss the prickle on her neck. But the sound... it was distinct. Not a creak, not a groan. It was the sound of someone walking, slowly, deliberately. Shuffling. It echoed in the vast quiet, a sound that seemed to consume all other noise.
visuals: The very end of a long, dark hospital corridor, a single, faint yellow light bulb hanging, casting long, wavering shadows, suggesting a figure just out of sight, 50mm lens.
A close-up of a dusty, peeling hospital wall, a shadow of a hand (not a human hand) reaching out, indistinct, with soft focus on the texture of the wall.

scenes.narration: A few nights later, the shuffle returned. And with it, a new sound. A soft, metallic jingle. Like a heavy bunch of keys, swaying with each slow, deliberate step. Ruvini felt her stomach clench. Keys. Who would be carrying keys like that, at this hour, in this empty ward? She leaned out from the nurses' station, straining her ears. The jingle grew a fraction louder, then softer, as if passing a doorway, then returning. It wasn't regular, not like a guard's confident stride. This was... hesitant. Lingering. The air in the corridor, usually cool, now felt profoundly cold, a pocket of unnatural chill that made the tiny hairs on her arms stand up.
visuals: An old, heavy ring of metal keys, slightly rusted, hanging from a hook on a dark wooden panel, a faint jingle suggested by motion blur, shallow depth of field, close-up.
Ruvini's back, a slight, tense curve to her shoulders, as she peers down a long, dark corridor from the safety of the nurses' station doorway, a single fluorescent tube flickering above her head.

scenes.narration: At dawn, exhausted and unnerved, Ruvini found Nurse Leela. "The shuffling... the keys," she whispered, pouring herself a cup of steaming tea. Leela just nodded slowly, stirring sugar into her own cup. "Ah, the Doctor's Midnight Rounds. They say it's Dr. Samarawickrama, the old superintendent. Died in the hospital itself, you know. A dedicated man. Couldn't let go of his patients, even in death." Leela's voice was soft, devoid of dramatics, as if speaking of a living colleague. "He checks on his wards. Some say he pauses at the rooms of those who suffered most. A final visit." The tea felt scalding, but Ruvini shivered.
visuals: Two figures (backs to camera) at a simple tea stall outside the hospital grounds at dawn, steam rising from their cups, the red earth road visible, soft morning light, 35mm lens.
A wide shot of an empty hospital ward, with the early morning light casting long, serene shadows through the windows, but a subtle, unsettling emptiness remains.

scenes.narration: That night, the memory of Leela’s words hung heavy. Ruvini found herself listening, not just hearing. Her rounds felt different. Each shadow seemed deeper, each creak more sinister. When she finally reached Ward C, the vast, echoing space felt colder than usual. The air was still, heavy, like before a storm. She could almost feel the weight of eyes on her, though no one was there. The distant drone of temple drums from the city felt like a heartbeat, slow and deliberate, matching the cadence she now expected. She checked the rooms, her flashlight beam cutting through the inky blackness, revealing only empty beds and forgotten corners.
visuals: Ruvini, a small figure in a nurse's uniform, standing at the entrance to a cavernous, empty hospital ward, her flashlight beam cutting through the profound darkness, 24mm wide angle, deep shadows.
A close-up on an old, tarnished brass doorknob on a heavy wooden door, the wood scarred and dark, with a faint, almost invisible fingerprint smudge, suggesting a recent touch.

scenes.narration: Then, at the far end of the longest corridor, where the emergency light barely flickered, she saw it. A silhouette. Tall, broad-shouldered. Dressed in what looked like an old-fashioned doctor's coat. It was moving, slowly, with that tell-tale shuffle. The jingle of keys, unmistakable now, followed its every movement. Her breath hitched. Ruvini pressed herself against the wall, behind a medical cart, her heart hammering against her ribs. It wasn't a trick of the light. It wasn't her imagination. This was the Doctor. Real, tangible in its spectral presence, moving with a chilling, silent purpose.
visuals: A long, dimly lit hospital corridor, flickering fluorescent lights, a lone, indistinct silhouette of a man in an old-fashioned coat at the far end, his back to the viewer, casting an unnerving shadow, 50mm lens.
A low-angle shot, looking up at the ceiling of the corridor, where a single, old fluorescent light tube flickers erratically, casting jumpy shadows that seem to distort the space.

scenes.narration: The figure shuffled closer, step by agonizing step. The jingle of the keys, a macabre accompaniment to its phantom patrol, grew louder. Ruvini squeezed her eyes shut for a second, then forced them open. It was real. Too real. The Doctor, they called him. Dr. Samarawickrama. He paused. Right in front of a particular doorway, a room that had always felt... heavier than the others. A room that was always kept empty. He stood there for a long moment, head slightly bowed, as if deep in thought, or perhaps, listening. Then, with another soft jingle, he continued his slow, endless patrol down the corridor, eventually fading into the deep shadows at the turn.
visuals: A ghostly silhouette of a man in an old-fashioned coat, paused at the threshold of a specific, old wooden door, his head slightly tilted as if listening, long shadows, soft focus, 85mm lens.
Ruvini (from behind) crouched low behind a medical trolley in a dark corridor, her figure small and vulnerable, watching the distant silhouette of the doctor, 24mm wide angle, dramatic lighting.

scenes.narration: The sounds faded. The jingle died away. But the cold remained. A lingering, profound chill in the very spot where the Doctor had paused. Ruvini stayed hidden for what felt like an eternity, listening to the frantic thumping of her own heart. When she finally dared to move, her legs felt like lead. She approached the doorway where he had stood. There was nothing visible, no trace. Only that unnatural cold spot, a lingering echo of a presence. The air itself felt thick, heavy with unspoken sadness and eternal duty. The memory of that silhouette, the shuffle, the keys… it etched itself into her mind, a permanent cold mark.
visuals: A close-up of an old, wooden doorframe, the paint chipped and faded, with a palpable sense of cold air emanating from the dark space beyond, soft, diffused light, 100mm macro lens.
Ruvini's hand (from behind, not showing face) slowly reaching out to touch the cold, ancient wall of the corridor where the doctor stood, a sense of trepidation, soft, atmospheric lighting.

scenes.narration: Ruvini finished her shift that morning, a quiet resolve in her eyes. She never questioned the stories again. She became one of the staff who simply accepted the Doctor's Midnight Rounds as part of Angoda's night. Sometimes, on those quiet nights, she'd still hear the shuffling, the faint jingle. She wouldn't be afraid, not truly. Just respectful. It was his hospital, after all. His patients. His duty. And some duties, my friends, never truly end. Even when the body has long turned to dust. If you've enjoyed this glimpse into Angoda's whispers, do consider following Ceylon Dread for more stories from our island's shadows.
visuals: Early morning light filtering through the high, barred windows of an old hospital corridor, casting long, peaceful stripes across the floor, a sense of quiet resignation, 35mm lens.
Ruvini, seen from behind, standing by a window, looking out at the red earth road and distant jak trees as the sun rises over the hospital grounds, a quiet moment of reflection, cinematic light.

shorts.title: The Doctor's Midnight Rounds: A Chilling Jingle
shorts.narration: Have you ever heard a sound that didn't belong? In the quiet of Angoda's old hospital wards, Ruvini, a new nurse, started hearing it. A faint, dragging shuffle. At first, she dismissed it. Just the old building settling, she thought, trying to calm her racing heart. But then came the jingle. A soft, metallic sound, like heavy keys, swaying with each slow, deliberate step. It wasn't the guards. No one else was on this desolate ward at this hour. The sound grew clearer, closer, echoing in the vast, empty space. Ruvini pressed herself against the wall, her breath catching in her throat, as the chilling jingle kept coming closer... Vertical shot: A close-up of Ruvini's trembling hand gripping a metal medical cart, her knuckles white, in a dimly lit corridor.

Vertical shot: A silhouette of a doorframe at the end of a corridor, with a subtle, indistinct movement just beyond it.
Vertical shot: Ruvini's back, a small figure, pressed against a cold, peeling hospital wall, looking down a dark corridor.

shorts.title: Angoda's Phantom Patrol: The Superintendent's Visit
shorts.narration: Some shadows aren't just shadows. In Angoda's haunted corridors, a young nurse named Ruvini learned this chilling truth. She'd heard whispers of Dr. Samarawickrama, the long-dead superintendent, still making his midnight rounds. And then, she saw him. A tall, indistinct silhouette, dressed in an old-fashioned doctor's coat, shuffling slowly down the longest corridor. The jingle of his phantom keys, a familiar horror now. Ruvini watched, frozen, as the figure approached a specific, empty doorway. It paused there, head slightly bowed, as if observing an invisible patient, or perhaps, listening for something only it could hear. And then, it stopped, right outside my door... The full story is on our channel.
visuals: Vertical shot: A long, dark hospital corridor, a lone, spectral silhouette of a man in an old-fashioned coat at the very end, barely visible.
Vertical shot: A close-up of an old, heavy wooden door, scarred and dark, with a rusty handle, standing slightly ajar.
Vertical shot: A subtle, ghostly reflection of a man's silhouette in a polished linoleum floor, barely perceptible, in a dark corridor.
Vertical shot: Ruvini's face, partially obscured by shadow, her eyes wide with fear and disbelief, looking out from behind a pillar.
Vertical shot: A very narrow shot of the space between an old door and its frame, with deep, unsettling darkness within the room.
